hints: Focus on what type of product a primary halogenoalkane gives when Br is replaced by a nucleophile that can later be oxidised.
Remember that heating 1-bromopropane with aqueous NaOH gives propan-1-ol, a primary alcohol.
Think about what happens when you oxidise a primary alcohol strongly, first to an aldehyde and then one step further.
walkthrough:
**Identify the nucleophilic substitution product**

Think of 1-bromopropane as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. With aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ heated, $\text{OH}^-$ replaces $\text{Br}$ by nucleophilic substitution.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Br}^-$$
So we make propan-1-ol, a primary alcohol.

**Oxidise the primary alcohol**

A primary alcohol can be oxidised in two stages with acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ under reflux. It first gives an aldehyde, then a carboxylic acid.

Oxidation sequence:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
The final product with the same 3-carbon chain is propanoic acid.

**Match to R**

Compound R is formed after both steps are complete, so it must be the carboxylic acid, not the intermediate alcohol or aldehyde. That points clearly to propanoic acid.

options.A: Correct. Nucleophilic substitution gives propan-1-ol, and strong oxidation of this primary alcohol gives propanal then propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$. The carbon chain stays at 3 carbons throughout.
options.B: Incorrect. Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone made by oxidising a secondary alcohol like propan-2-ol. Starting from 1-bromopropane we get a primary alcohol, which cannot give a ketone.
options.C: Incorrect. Propylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, is made by nucleophilic substitution with ammonia, but it cannot be oxidised to give R in this scheme. The question requires substitution followed by oxidation, which points to an alcohol to acid route.
options.D: Incorrect. Propyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is an ester made by reacting an alcohol with a carboxylic acid. It is not formed by simple substitution then oxidation, and it has 5 carbons, not 3.
